newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Winter kills 20 in Romania, blocks road and rail.
newsitem.headline: Winter kills 20 in Romania, blocks road and rail.

text.p: About 20 people have frozen to death in bitter cold and blizzards that disrupted rail and road traffic in Romania, officials said on Sunday.

Government general secretary Remus Opris told state radio 20 people had frozen to death in record low temperatures, some in the capital Bucharest and the government would provide three billion lei ($750,000) to help people affected by the weather.
Temperatures have touched minus 25 Celsius (minus 18 Fahrenheit) in the last three days, with heavy snowfalls and blizzards disrupting rail, road traffic and shipping.
Transport Minister Traian Basescu told a news conference traffic had resumed on main roads and railways and the main Black Sea port of Constanta had reopened.
"We had cases when railway tracks cracked because of the low temperatures. There were no accidents," Basescu said.
But he added that rail and road traffic remained a "problem" in south-eastern and eastern Romania.
"Our teams there clean the roads round the clock but snow blocks traffic again in minutes," he said, adding that the military were assisting in Constanta and Braila counties.
A Bucharest police source told Reuters the victims of the cold were mainly elderly, homeless people or beggars.
Unconfirmed reports in the local media on Sunday put the number of fatalities from the cold at 24 in Bucharest alone. Mortuary officials were not available for comment.
Beggars and homeless people have become a common sight around Romanian railway stations, hotels, restaurants and shops.
Official figures are not available for the total number or homeless or for the "street children" who sleep at night in Bucharest's sewers, parks or deserted buildings.
